title: OAuth callback reflects unescaped HTML from query and exception data
reasoning: The public browser callback inserts the OAuth error query parameter, token-exchange exception text, and configured label directly into HTML without escaping. A request such as /oauth/callback?error=<script>...</script> will be rendered inside the page, creating reflected XSS on an unauthenticated endpoint. Exception text may also contain remote/provider-controlled content and is rendered the same way.
reproduction: GET /oauth/callback?error=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C/script%3E returns an HTML page containing the script markup in the detail div.
recommendation: HTML-escape all dynamic values before formatting the templates, or render via a templating layer with autoescaping. Keep internal exception details out of the public page and log them server-side instead.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for GET /oauth/callback, and there is no evidence of a regression test asserting that callback HTML escapes user-controlled values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI TestClient test for GET /oauth/callback?error=<script>alert(1)</script> that asserts the response contains escaped text such as <script> and not a literal <script> tag.
minimumFixScope: Escape the dynamic values used by oauth_web_callback before passing them to ERROR_HTML.format and SUCCESS_HTML.format; optionally replace public exception text with a generic message.
